Remember the Hùng origins; keep the old crimson blood alive in our hearts.
This Giỗ Tổ, may the rivers and mountains endure and the descendants stay united.

gifts.title: A trip back to the roots
gifts.text: Take the family to the Hùng Temple or to your ancestral homeland.

gifts.title: Bánh chưng & bánh giầy
gifts.text: The traditional offering tray for the day at home.

gifts.title: History books
gifts.text: Books about the Hùng era for the younger generation.

holidays.name: Tết Thanh Minh (Tomb-Sweeping Day)
holidays.tagline: The season of remembering the graves — Vietnam's tomb-sweeping festival.
holidays.meaning: The festival of remembrance at the threshold of clear spring — when living descendants sweep the tombs, offer incense and renew the bond with their ancestors.

traditions.title: Tảo mộ — sweeping the tombs
traditions.text: Families return to their hometowns during Thanh minh week to tend the graves: clearing weeds, adding fresh earth, repairing headstones, cleaning incense bowls. The custom treats it as 'renovating the house' of the departed — many cemeteries now set shared hours to keep things tidy.

traditions.title: Offering incense & flowers
traditions.text: After the tidying, descendants light incense, lay fresh flowers and burn votive paper. Some families add boiled chicken, xôi and sweet soup; part of the tray is then laid upon the grave for the ancestors.

traditions.title: Family visits & spring walks
traditions.text: Thanh minh falls on the fifth solar term of spring — the year's clearest, brightest spell — so the tomb visit often ends with an outdoor meal or a family spring outing. The old saying calls it 'half tomb-sweeping, half spring-wandering'.

traditions.title: Sticky-rice dishes
traditions.text: Each region has its tomb-day foods: the North cooks xôi gấc and tro-tàu cakes with molasses; the Center makes bánh phu thê and chè kho; the South favors chè xoa xoa. Humble dishes, but anyone far from home misses their taste that week.

wishes: On Thanh Minh, may the ancestors bless your home with peace and health.
Remembering our roots — may your family be safe, whole and serene this Thanh Minh.
In this clear bright season, may your heart be light and your home at peace.
Wishing you a gentle Thanh Minh — honoring the past, treasuring the present.
May the ancestors watch over you and yours all year round.

gifts.title: Fresh flowers for the grave
gifts.text: Chrysanthemums, lilies or roses for the ancestors' graves and altar.

gifts.title: Incense & candles
gifts.text: A respectful bundle for the family tảo mộ visit.

gifts.title: Xôi & glutinous cakes
gifts.text: Traditional offerings many regions prepare for tomb-sweeping.

holidays.name: Reunification Day (April 30)
holidays.tagline: The day the country was reunified.
holidays.meaning: A day of independence, reunification, and gratitude to the generations who sacrificed for the country.

traditions.title: Flying the flag
traditions.text: Across the cities — above all the Lê Duẩn–Độc Lập axis in HCMC and the streets of Hanoi — red flags carpet entire streets through the April 30 week. Residents hang flags on their own homes as a quiet reminder of reunification day.

traditions.title: Commemorations & parades
traditions.text: In milestone years — the 40th (2015) and 50th (2025) anniversaries — state-level parades march through HCMC with tens of thousands of participants. The 50th-anniversary parade of April 30, 2025 ranked among the largest in Vietnamese history.

traditions.title: Back to the roots
traditions.text: Veteran families and youth delegations use the occasion to return to old battlefields — the Củ Chi tunnels, Quảng Trị, Trường Sơn — and visit martyrs' cemeteries. Unit reunions are held across the country by former soldiers.

wishes: Proud of April 30 — may our country forever enjoy peace and prosperity.
Honoring those who fell for the independence we have today.
May our country stay united and stride firmly into the future.
April 30 — the day the rivers and mountains became one again. Forever proud.
Today's peace is a promise to tomorrow. Happy Reunification Day.

gifts.title: A national flag
gifts.text: A small gold-star flag for the balcony on the big day.

gifts.title: A heritage trip
gifts.text: The Independence Palace or the Củ Chi tunnels for a trip back to the roots.

gifts.title: History books & films
gifts.text: Materials on the Hồ Chí Minh Campaign for the family.

holidays.name: International Workers' Day (May 1)
holidays.tagline: Honoring workers around the world.
holidays.meaning: A day recognizing the value of labor and the rightful rights of working people.

traditions.title: The April 30–May 1 break
traditions.text: The two back-to-back holidays form the year's longest break before summer — many families take a short trip or return to their hometowns. Beach destinations like Đà Nẵng, Nha Trang and Phú Quốc typically sell out a month ahead.

traditions.title: Honoring outstanding workers
traditions.text: Unions and companies commend skilled workers and improvement initiatives; newspapers run features on everyday labor — welders, rural doctors, mountain teachers. In recent years the 'pioneering worker' theme has been tied to digital transformation.

traditions.title: Union activities
traditions.text: Workers' Month (May) kicks off right after the holiday: trade-skills contests, factory football leagues, job counseling and reunion programs for migrant workers. Many industrial parks open discount 'workers' markets' around this time.

wishes: Wishing every worker a May 1 of real rest and real joy.
Grateful to the hands that build every value. Have a meaningful May Day!
May your work go smoothly and always be fairly rewarded.
Labor is glory — may you be rightly honored today.
May every diligent pair of hands harvest the sweetest fruit.

gifts.title: A short getaway
gifts.text: Make the most of the early-May break.

gifts.title: Health gifts
gifts.text: A massage pillow or a health check voucher for a worker.

gifts.title: A word of thanks
gifts.text: Sometimes a well-timed word of recognition is the best gift.

holidays.name: Mother's Day
holidays.tagline: One day of the year reserved just for Mom.
holidays.meaning: A day to say the words of love to Mom — the person standing behind every step we take.

traditions.title: Carnations for Mom
traditions.text: Carnations have belonged to this day since its founder — Anna Jarvis sent white carnations in memory of her late mother; pink and red ones now go to mothers still living. In Vietnam, roses, orchids and mixed bouquets are chosen just as often.

traditions.title: A meal cooked by the kids
traditions.text: The most praised gift on social media each year is a meal cooked by the children — even when it comes out a bit too salty or bland. Kids living far away order hotpot or braised chicken delivered so Mom can skip the kitchen for the day.

traditions.title: A call home
traditions.text: For those far from home, a video call asking 'have you eaten yet, Mom?' is the most on-time gift of all. Carriers even run call promotions for the occasion — many adults come to realize a weekly call outweighs any present.

wishes: Mom, you are the whole sky that shelters me. Happy Mother's Day!
May you always be healthy, peaceful and live long beside us.
Thank you, Mom, for giving me the whole world and asking nothing back.
On Mother's Day, I only wish you keep smiling as brightly as today.
Mom, I've grown up — but I still feel small in your arms.

gifts.title: Carnations
gifts.text: Red for love, white for remembrance.

gifts.title: Silk scarves & áo dài
gifts.text: A traditional gift every mother loves.

gifts.title: A full day off
gifts.text: Take over all the housework so Mom can truly rest.

holidays.name: International Children's Day
holidays.tagline: The day of little ones.
holidays.meaning: A day reminding society to protect, love and invest in the next generation.

traditions.title: Fun at school
traditions.text: On the morning of June 1 — often moved to the nearest weekend — kindergartens and primary schools hold festival days: folk games, performances by the kids themselves, year-end prizes. The 'school festival' memory is one of drums, water games and paper flowers.

traditions.title: Gifts for kids
traditions.text: Classic June 1 gifts are toys, comics and school bags — many parents now pick books and STEM kits instead of gadgets. Malls and toy stores set up play zones and week-long promotions for the occasion.

traditions.title: Charitable activities
traditions.text: Charities, children's funds and youth unions deliver gifts to disadvantaged kids — children's hospitals, SOS villages, flood-hit areas. Many fundraisers for underprivileged children's Tết also kick off around this season.

wishes: Happy June 1 — may you have fun, stay good and study well, little ones!
Wishing our little love health and lots of laughter every day.
Childhood comes only once — may yours be a Children's Day to remember.
May every little one be loved and free to be themselves.
Have a wonderful June 1 — today the whole world belongs to you, kids.

gifts.title: Picture & story books
gifts.text: A gift that's both fun and builds a reading habit.

gifts.title: Creative toys
gifts.text: Blocks, crafts and art supplies for little hands.

gifts.title: A day out
gifts.text: The park, the zoo or the movies with the whole family.

holidays.name: Vietnamese Family Day
holidays.tagline: Every Vietnamese person's warm nest.
holidays.meaning: A reminder to treasure your warm nest — the place where every journey begins and returns.

traditions.title: A family dinner
traditions.text: The day has no fixed rite — its 'rite' is simply the whole family eating together, a reminder of the shared dinner table amid busy lives. The culture ministry once campaigned for a phone-free 'family dinner hour' from 6 to 7:30 pm.

traditions.title: Family photos
traditions.text: Many families mark the day with a photo set — at a studio, in a park, or just a selfie around the dinner table. TV specials and 'happy family' photo contests are usually held around June 28.

traditions.title: Stories across generations
traditions.text: Family Day is when grandparents tell old stories and open the wedding album and family tree — a 'family tradition' session there is rarely time for otherwise. Many schools assign 'interview your grandparents' homework this week.

wishes: May our family always stay close, loving and at peace.
Home is where we return — may your warm nest always be cozy.
On Family Day, may every home be full of laughter.
May your nest always have someone waiting and a hot meal ready.
Family is the anchor — may our home stay warm forever.

gifts.title: A family photo album
gifts.text: Print the shared moments into something you can hold.

gifts.title: A full dinner
gifts.text: Book a table or cook a complete family meal at home.

gifts.title: A trip together
gifts.text: A nearby weekend picnic for the whole family.

holidays.name: War Invalids & Martyrs' Day
holidays.tagline: Repaying the debt of gratitude.
holidays.meaning: A day to honor those who traded blood and bone for today's peace.

traditions.title: Visiting martyrs' cemeteries
traditions.text: Millions visit their local martyrs' cemetery during the July 27 week — lighting incense, wiping headstones, reading the names aloud. In Quảng Trị, the great Trường Sơn and Đường 9 cemeteries welcome the year's largest gatherings of gray-haired veterans.

traditions.title: Visiting policy families
traditions.text: The 'repaying gratitude' spirit becomes concrete work: localities, businesses and schools visit Heroic Mothers, wounded veterans and martyrs' families — bringing gifts, repairing 'gratitude houses' and delivering insurance papers.

traditions.title: Candles of gratitude
traditions.text: On the evening of July 26, candle-lighting ceremonies spread from national cemeteries to village shrines — thousands of flames lit at the same hour. The 'sea of candles' at Trường Sơn cemetery is among the year's most moving sights.

wishes: Forever grateful to the heroic martyrs of our nation.
There is peace today because yesterday there were those who never came home.
Repaying the debt of gratitude — respectfully honoring people of merit.
We bow our heads to the sacrifices that gave today the name 'peace'.
Gratitude is never enough — honoring our nation's heroes.

gifts.title: Care gifts
gifts.text: Rice, milk and supplements for a war-invalid family nearby.

gifts.title: Flowers for the memorial
gifts.text: A wreath or bouquet laid at the local martyrs' memorial.

gifts.title: Donations to gratitude funds
gifts.text: Helping build 'houses of gratitude' for people of merit.

holidays.name: Vu Lan Festival
holidays.tagline: The season of filial devotion.
holidays.meaning: A season to remember the debt to one's parents and repay those who gave us life.

traditions.title: Pinning a rose on the chest
traditions.text: The custom of pinning a rose at the Vu Lan service — red for those whose mother lives, white for those whose mother has passed — was started by Zen master Thích Nhất Hạnh in Huế in 1962. More than half a century on, the small flower is the day's most familiar image.

traditions.title: Vu Lan at the pagoda
traditions.text: On the seventh full moon, pagodas hold the filial-piety service: chanting, rose-pinning, and teachings on parents' sacrifice from the Ullambana Sutra — the story of Mục Kiền Liên saving his mother. The busiest services fall on the full moon or the nearest Sunday.

traditions.title: 7th-month full-moon offerings
traditions.text: Alongside the temple rite, families lay a full-moon tray for ancestors — many add an outdoor 'wandering souls' tray at dusk with thin rice soup, salt and votive money. Feeding lost souls shares the day's spirit of compassion.

wishes: This Vu Lan season, may your parents always be healthy and at peace.
As long as Mom and Dad live, we have the whole world — treasure every day beside them.
May the debt of birth and raising be repaid with filial love each day.
Vu Lan returns — praying for those who gave us life.
In this season of devotion, may your parents always be safe and well.

gifts.title: A Vu Lan rose
gifts.text: A small red rose to pin on your chest on the day.

gifts.title: A filial gift
gifts.text: Supplements, milk — or simply a visit home.

gifts.title: Vegetarian sweets
gifts.text: Light treats for the meatless full-moon tray.

holidays.name: Vietnam National Day (September 2)
holidays.tagline: The day the nation was born.
holidays.meaning: A day of national pride and the aspiration for peace and development.

traditions.title: September 2 parades
traditions.text: In milestone years — the 70th (2015) and 80th (2025) anniversaries — parades fill Ba Đình Square, the very spot where the Declaration of Independence was read. The A80 parade of 2025 gathered tens of thousands of troops and civilians and was broadcast live nationwide.

traditions.title: Fireworks
traditions.text: On the night of September 2, Hanoi and HCMC launch fireworks at multiple points — the Han River bridge in Đà Nẵng offers the country's most spectacular show. Since 2022 many provinces have swapped high-altitude fireworks for drone light displays.

traditions.title: Streets of flags
traditions.text: From late August the national flag blankets the streets — even the smallest alleys turn red as residents hang flags on their own homes. Photos of flag-lined streets around the Opera House and the Old Quarter are the holiday's signature image.

wishes: Proud to be Vietnamese! Happy National Day, September 2.
May our country forever keep its independence, freedom and happiness.
Celebrating the day the Fatherland was born — united and firm toward the future.
From Ba Đình that day to today — proud of Vietnam.
May our brocade land stay forever majestic and flourishing.

gifts.title: Flags & September 2 gear
gifts.text: Small flags and red flag t-shirts for the parade day.

gifts.title: A trip to the roots
gifts.text: Visit the Imperial Citadel, the Hồ Chí Minh Mausoleum, or his homeland in Nghệ An.

gifts.title: Books about Uncle Hồ
gifts.text: Meaningful historical materials for the younger generation.

holidays.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
holidays.tagline: The reunion festival under the moon.
holidays.meaning: The full-moon night of togetherness — adults missing home, children dreaming of star lanterns.

traditions.title: Breaking the feast under the moon
traditions.text: On the full-moon night, the feast tray holds a pomelo carved like a boat, a banana bunch and mooncakes arranged in patterns — children 'break the feast' near midnight for luck. Adults sip tea and watch the moon while kids argue over the pomelo-boat's tail.

traditions.title: Star-lantern parades
traditions.text: Star lanterns of colored cellophane, carp lanterns, pull-string troop lanterns — bands of children parade hand-held lights through the alleys on the full-moon night. Musical battery lanterns are common now, but Hội An and the old quarters still keep the paper ones.

traditions.title: Lion dances
traditions.text: Lion-dance troupes work through the neighborhoods to thundering drums, performing for 'lucky treats' hung in front of shops — the drumbeat announces Mid-Autumn's arrival. Children chase the lions until late, a shared childhood memory across generations.

wishes: Happy Mid-Autumn! May your family be reunited under the full moon.
Wishing the little ones a season bright with star lanterns.
The moon is round, the people are gathered — wishing you a warm Mid-Autumn.
May this moon season bring you fullness, like the light of the full moon.
Mid-Autumn is here — may every home gather and every child laugh.

gifts.title: Mooncakes
gifts.text: Baked or snow-skin cakes with lotus seed or green tea filling are classics.

gifts.title: A lantern for the kids
gifts.text: Handmade star lanterns and carp lanterns.

gifts.title: Lotus tea
gifts.text: A tea-and-cake pair for the moonlit reunion.

holidays.name: Vietnamese Women's Day
holidays.tagline: Honoring the women of Vietnam.
holidays.meaning: The day reserved for Vietnamese women — honoring their sacrifices, resilience and beauty.

traditions.title: Flowers & gifts
traditions.text: As on March 8, flowers and gifts flow to mothers, wives and sisters — but October 20 is 'our own day', purely Vietnamese. Flower markets and gift shops peak on the evening of the 19th and the morning of the 20th.

traditions.title: Honoring exemplary women
traditions.text: The day is tied to the founding of the Vietnam Women's Union on October 20, 1930. Offices hold gatherings commending Heroic Mothers, female scientists and businesswomen all through the week.

traditions.title: Men in the kitchen
traditions.text: A modern custom: on October 20 husbands cook dinner and sons wash the dishes — a meal made by men is the most practical gift. 'Vietnamese men in the kitchen on October 20' has quietly become a beloved new tradition.

wishes: Happy October 20 — may you always be beautiful, happy and loved!
20/10 — may the women of Vietnam stay radiant and successful.
Thank you to the wonderful women in my life.
Wishing you an October 20 full of nothing but flowers, gifts and laughter.
20/10 — may you always be the most beautiful flower in Vietnam's garden.

gifts.title: Fresh flowers
gifts.text: A bouquet with a handwritten card is always the first choice.

gifts.title: An áo dài
gifts.text: The flowing tunic — the symbol of Vietnamese women's beauty.

gifts.title: Self-care gifts
gifts.text: A spa session, cosmetics, or a dinner date.

holidays.name: Vietnamese Teachers' Day
holidays.tagline: Respecting teachers and the way of learning.
holidays.meaning: One letter learned, a teacher for life — the day to remember those who guided us.

traditions.title: Students giving flowers
traditions.text: Before class on November 20, the class monitor presents a bouquet and a card of thanks; many schools hold a short ceremony first period. Younger pupils draw cards, high-schoolers buy flowers, university students send thank-you videos.

traditions.title: Alumni visits
traditions.text: On this day, old class cohorts — from retirees to fresh graduates — return to visit their former teachers with flowers, cakes and old keepsakes. The 'three generations of teacher and students' reunion is the day's most familiar scene.

traditions.title: Messages of thanks
traditions.text: Lately, instead of expensive gifts, parents encourage handwritten notes — 'teachers only need a sincere thank you'. Education authorities also regularly remind everyone of a 'no-material-gifts' November 20 to keep the day clean and meaningful.

wishes: Wishing teachers a November 20 of health, happiness and lasting devotion.
Thank you, teachers, for lighting the fire of knowledge in me.
On Teachers' Day, I respectfully wish you stay forever young and joyful.
The debt of teaching is heavy as a long river — wishing you health, teachers.
May those who grow people harvest sweet fruit all their lives.

gifts.title: Flowers & thank-you cards
gifts.text: Simple, sincere and true to tradition.

gifts.title: Books & a fine pen
gifts.text: Gifts that suit the profession of growing people.

gifts.title: A surprise visit
gifts.text: Drop in on an old teacher — a gift everyone treasures.

holidays.name: Vietnam People's Army Day
holidays.tagline: The traditional day of a heroic army.
holidays.meaning: Honoring the soldiers who have kept — and keep — the country's independence and sovereignty.

traditions.title: Traditional reunions
traditions.text: Veterans of each unit — regiments, companies, the famous 'floating battalions' — reunite around December 22, reading the roll of fallen comrades and singing old marching songs. The date doubles as the nationwide All-People's Defense Festival in localities.

traditions.title: Commending soldiers
traditions.text: Units mark the day with ceremonies commending outstanding soldiers under the motto 'excellent at duty, devoted at home' — young conscripts cooking a meal for policy families is a familiar image of the day.

traditions.title: Border activities
traditions.text: Army Day comes with 'for the borderlands, for the fishermen' work: donating comradeship houses, free clinics in border districts, 'spring at the frontier' exchanges. Naval units begin receiving 'Tết on the islands' gift shipments around this date.

wishes: Happy Vietnam People's Army Day, December 22!
Honoring the soldiers who stand guard over the nation's peaceful sleep.
Respectfully wishing our servicemen strength under calm skies and seas.
Thank you to those who traded their youth for the Fatherland's peace.
22/12 — may our heroic army stay forever steadfast and loyal.

gifts.title: Flowers & letters
gifts.text: Send thanks to loved ones serving in the military.

gifts.title: Gifts for far-away soldiers
gifts.text: Food and handwritten letters to troops on the borders and islands.

gifts.title: Military history books
gifts.text: Materials on the nation's heroic campaigns.

holidays.name: Christmas
holidays.tagline: The warmest, most peaceful season of the year.
holidays.meaning: The season of giving, peace and warm moments beside loved ones.

traditions.title: Church on Christmas Eve
traditions.text: On Christmas Eve the great cathedrals — St. Joseph's in Hanoi, Notre-Dame in HCMC, Phủ Cam in Huế — overflow with visitors, including many non-Christians who come to watch the midnight mass. A religious service turned street festival: that is Vietnam's signature Christmas.

traditions.title: Exchanging gifts
traditions.text: Santas hand out gifts in malls and parks while kids go 'Santa hunting' on Christmas Eve. Families exchange presents under the tree on the morning of the 25th; classes and offices play Secret Santa.

traditions.title: Decorating the tree
traditions.text: Christmas trees — real or 3–10 m artificial ones — go up in front of churches, hotels and walking streets from early December. The nativity grotto recreating the Bethlehem manger is a distinctly Vietnamese touch: each parish and family competes to build the street's grandest.

wishes: Merry Christmas! Wishing you a peaceful, warm Christmas.
May the season bring you plenty of joy.
A peaceful Christmas — may every good thing come to your family.
A peaceful Noel — may you be embraced by the people who love you.
May your holiday season be warm enough to carry you through winter.

gifts.title: Christmas gifts for kids
gifts.text: Wrapped toys left under the tree.

gifts.title: Wool scarves & gloves
gifts.text: Warm gifts for the chilly end of the year.

gifts.title: Cookies & chocolate
gifts.text: A sweet gift box for friends and colleagues.

holidays.name: Kitchen Gods' Day (Ông Công Ông Táo)
holidays.tagline: Sending the Kitchen Gods back to heaven.
holidays.meaning: Kitchen Gods' Day is the handover between the old year and the new — the day families tidy the hearth, honor the flame that kept them warm all year, and trust that good deeds will be carried to heaven. It is also a reminder to live kindly inside our own homes.

traditions.title: Seeing off the Táo quân
traditions.text: At noon on the 23rd of the last lunar month, every home lays a send-off tray for the Kitchen Gods — betel, wine, sticky rice, sometimes red paper hats and votive money. After the rite, the hats and paper money are burned, 'dispatched to the Jade Emperor' with the incense smoke.

traditions.title: Releasing carp
traditions.text: By legend the carp transforms into a dragon and carries the Kitchen Gods to heaven — so after the offering many families buy red carp to release into rivers and lakes. Amid recent debate about releasing fish into natural waterways, many now release into private ponds or simply offer paper carp.

traditions.title: Cleaning the house
traditions.text: Once the Kitchen Gods depart, the house is 'free of spirits' — the perfect moment for the final clean: dusting cobwebs, repairing the altar, replacing incense bowls, a deep clean before Tết. The folk logic is really a clever nudge to get the whole house ready for the New Year.

traditions.title: Offerings to the Earth God
traditions.text: Alongside the kitchen's Táo quân, the household also offers to the Earth God — the deity guarding the land of the home — with its own or a shared tray. The saying 'first the Kitchen God, second the Earth God' recalls the two closest deities in a Vietnamese house, both sent off this night.

wishes: May your home's hearth stay warm and full of love all year!
The Táo quân fly to heaven with good news — wishing your family peace as Tết arrives!
Carp leaping the dragon gate — may everything flow smoothly in the new year!
May grandparents and parents stay healthy, and every home gather at year's end!
May next year's hearth always burn warm and the rice bowl stay full!
Send the Táo to the sky, welcome fortune home — wishing a prosperous new year!

gifts.title: A Táo quân offering set
gifts.text: Táo hats and a vegetarian or meat tray — the main offerings of the 23rd of the last month.

gifts.title: Carp to release
gifts.text: Live carp to release into ponds — the day's most spiritual item.

gifts.title: Gifts for the family
gifts.text: Mai or đào blossoms and Tết sweets — the Tết atmosphere begins today.

holidays.name: Tết Hàn Thực (Cold Food Festival)
holidays.tagline: The festival of floating-rice and mung-bean cakes.
holidays.meaning: Tết Hàn thực is a day of vegetarian food, remembering one's roots and practicing purity in the new year — a quiet note in the string of post-Tết festivals, when people offer their ancestors little round cakes of sweet clarity.

traditions.title: Cooking bánh trôi & bánh chay
traditions.text: From the afternoon of the 2nd, families shape little bánh trôi with sugar-cube centers and fist-sized bánh chay with mung-bean filling — they are done when they float. The trôi go into ginger sweet soup, the chay onto their own plate; most kitchens make enough for offerings and for sharing.

traditions.title: Ancestor offerings
traditions.text: On the morning of the 3rd, the trôi-and-chay tray replaces fruit on the altar — a rite preserving the 'cold food' origin of the festival. Families believe ancestors receive the new season's blessing through these soft white cakes.

traditions.title: A vegetarian day
traditions.text: Many families eat vegetarian on the 3rd of the third month — cleansing in early spring and recalling the old 'day without fire' that allowed only cold food. Still, in Vietnam the day is remembered most for its two sweet floating cakes.

traditions.title: Pagoda visits
traditions.text: Many households choose the day for a pagoda visit or one last spring outing before routine resumes after the first full moon. Children remember the 3rd of the third month for 'floating cakes' — the sweet soup grandparents never fail to cook.

wishes: Wishing your family a sweet and serene Hàn thực day!
Round bánh trôi — may your life be full and sweet!
May grandparents and parents stay healthy and warm through every spring!
May every home grow closer and every heart grow kinder!
A peaceful Hàn thực — wishing you a year of safety and quiet mind!

gifts.title: Bánh trôi & bánh chay
gifts.text: A box of floating and mung-bean cakes — the traditional gift for the 3rd of the 3rd month.

gifts.title: Lotus tea & vegetarian sweets
gifts.text: Lotus-scented tea and pure sweets suiting a vegetarian day.

gifts.title: Offering flowers
gifts.text: A lotus or white chrysanthemum bouquet for the family altar.

holidays.name: Tết Đoan Ngọ (Pest-Killing Festival)
holidays.tagline: High noon at its peak — the pest-killing festival.
holidays.meaning: Tết Đoan Ngọ is Vietnam's folk answer to the turn of summer: a day of cleansing the body, protecting health, and staying close to mothers and children — for the pest-killing custom is also the custom of preserving the home's vitality.

traditions.title: Eating sour fruits
traditions.text: Thanh trà plums, sấu dracontomelum, mulberries — the sour early-summer fruits are the 'pest-killers' of Đoan Ngọ. Folk practice has them eaten early in the morning on an empty stomach, 'cleansing the insides' before breakfast.

traditions.title: Glutinous-rice wine
traditions.text: Rượu nếp — fermented golden-flower sticky rice rolled into little balls — is the must-have of the 5th-day noon meal; its sweet warmth is said to burn off the last parasites. Children get the cooked version; adults take the raw wine with a pinch of sesame salt and chili.

traditions.title: Gathering noon herbs
traditions.text: Between 11 am and 1 pm on the 5th — the Hour of the Horse on the Day of the Horse in the Month of the Horse — yang energy is believed to peak, making herbs picked then the most potent. People once gathered mugwort and bamboo leaves to dry for year-round remedies.

traditions.title: Burning vía & five-color threads
traditions.text: At dusk some places used to burn small vía fires at the gate to 'drive off pests' — rare today for safety. But the customs of airing clothes in the sun and hanging mugwort by the door still carry the old spirit of cleansing at the start of summer.

wishes: A healthy Đoan Ngọ — may your family have a happy, ailment-free summer!
The fruits ripen in season — may your life ripen sweet and full!
Wishing Mom good health — a child's devotion circles you always!
At noon at its peak — may your energy overflow and illness retreat!
May every home stay cool and every heart peaceful in mid-summer!

gifts.title: A fresh fruit basket
gifts.text: Lychee, plum, green mango — the exact ritual of pest-killing.

gifts.title: Cơm rượu nếp
gifts.text: A box of homemade fermented rice — a meaningful traditional dish.

gifts.title: A five-color thread bracelet
gifts.text: A little traditional charm for children to ward off evil.

holidays.name: Vietnamese Doctors' Day
holidays.tagline: Honoring those who heal.
holidays.meaning: Vietnamese Doctors' Day is when the whole country says thank you to those who hold the scalpel and those who keep the night watch in emergency rooms — professions demanding both talent and compassion. 'A good physician must be like a loving mother' is that profession's living standard.

traditions.title: Flowers for doctors
traditions.text: On February 27 hospitals fill with flowers — recovered patients return with bouquets and thank-you letters for the doctors who saved them; medical students honor their mentors. Roses and lilies are the two most chosen blooms.

traditions.title: Ceremonies at hospitals
traditions.text: Hospitals from Việt Đức and Chợ Rẫy down to district clinics hold tradition gatherings: new doctors recite the Hippocratic oath, 'meritorious physicians' are honored, and retired teachers are thanked.

traditions.title: Free clinics
traditions.text: Around this day, volunteer medical teams run free check-ups in remote highlands — dispensing medicine, ultrasounds and charity eye surgeries. The profession calls it 'the most beautiful work of our own day'.

traditions.title: Tributes in the press
traditions.text: Newspapers and TV devote special features to doctors: the night-shift emergency physician, the 'jungle doctor' who fought malaria for thirty years, the female doctor in the mountains. These stories each February 27 bring medicine closer to the public.

wishes: Wishing our healers health — to save even more lives!
Thank you, doctors, for watching the nights like parents — may your kind hearts stay ever fresh!
May the white-coat people be safe — your families always wait for you!
Honoring a noble profession — may our healers be healthy and peaceful!
May Vietnam's health sector grow ever stronger and more compassionate!

gifts.title: Carnations
gifts.text: A pink carnation bouquet — the flower of respect for healers.

gifts.title: A thank-you card
gifts.text: A handwritten card to the family doctor or familiar clinic.

gifts.title: Wellness gifts
gifts.text: Tea, honey, vitamins — practical gifts for those who keep the night shifts.

holidays.name: Vietnam Revolutionary Press Day
holidays.tagline: Honoring those who wield the pen.
holidays.meaning: Vietnam Revolutionary Press Day honors the journalist — the profession that runs against the flood, goes down into the tunnels and writes with fairness. From the 1925 Thanh Niên newspaper to today's parliament, the press remains an organ of social democracy.

traditions.title: Press awards
traditions.text: Around June 21 comes journalism's biggest award season — the Golden Hammer & Sickle Prize and the National Press Awards — honoring investigations, anti-corruption reporting and the year's most striking press photography.

traditions.title: Journalists' gatherings
traditions.text: Journalists' associations and newsrooms hold tradition meetings: honoring veteran reporters, issuing new membership cards, and recalling June 21, 1925 — when Nguyễn Ái Quốc founded the newspaper Thanh Niên.

traditions.title: Press exhibitions
traditions.text: The national press exhibition and spring newspaper fairs display award-winning work alongside historic front pages — from Hán-script colonial papers to modern digital newsrooms. The day lets readers see the 'workshop' behind the news.

traditions.title: Talks on the craft
traditions.text: Panels around the day discuss digital transformation, AI in the newsroom and press ethics in the era of fake news — the hottest questions facing the profession at each stage.

wishes: May our journalists keep the fire of fairness — may the pen stay firm!
Honoring those who record history — may our reporters stay safe on the road!
May Vietnamese press stay truthful, humane and ever-renewing!
Wishing the revolutionary pen-wielders health and creative freedom within the bounds of truth!
Thank you for the pages that keep a community awake — may journalism shine on!

gifts.title: Journalism books
gifts.text: Books on the writing craft and fine press collections — for journalists and lovers of words.

gifts.title: A signature pen
gifts.text: A fine pen — the elegant symbol of the writing profession.

gifts.title: Flowers of tribute
gifts.text: A fresh bouquet for the reporters and editors you know.

holidays.name: Vietnamese Senior Citizens' Day
holidays.tagline: Respect the old, receive long life.
holidays.meaning: Senior Citizens' Day is when we bow before the silver-haired: grandparents, parents — the people who walked through war and hardship and built our families. 'Respect the old, receive long life' is not a ritual but a standard of living.

traditions.title: Longevity celebrations
traditions.text: Mừng thọ ceremonies mark the milestones of 60 (the returning cycle), 70, 77 ('joyful longevity'), 80, 88 ('rice longevity'), 90, 99 and 100 — descendants gather to present betel, red áo dài and congratulatory couplets. Many families fold the celebration into Tết or the October 1 occasion.

traditions.title: Visiting the elderly
traditions.text: Local Elderly Associations go door to door gifting citizens turning 80, 90 and 100 — milk, warm blankets, envelopes with wishes of long life; every commune keeps its own 'map of elders' so no household is missed.

traditions.title: Senior club activities
traditions.text: Elderly clubs are the real playground of rural seniors: poetry, chess, qigong, folk dance — many hold 'talented elder' contests around October 1. In the cities the day pairs with 'living healthy, living joyful' campaigns.

traditions.title: Children coming home
traditions.text: October 1 falls on an early-autumn weekend window — many children working far away pick it to come home and celebrate their grandparents. The 'day of grandparents' is also a nudge for the young to call their elders more often.

wishes: Wishing our grandparents a hundred years of life and a tranquil heart!
May you stay healthy, Grandmother — forever the sheltering tree of your grandchildren!
Wishing our parents more peaceful years beside their children!
Happy longevity — may every day be joyful and every year be happy!
Honoring the silver-haired — may the elderly be loved and cared for!

gifts.title: Nutritious foods
gifts.text: Bird's nest, milk, nuts — practical health gifts for the elderly.

gifts.title: Warm clothes & blankets
gifts.text: Sweaters and warm blankets for the elders' winter.

gifts.title: A family album
gifts.text: A photo book of the children — the most precious spiritual gift for grandparents.

holidays.name: Vietnamese Entrepreneurs' Day
holidays.tagline: Honoring the spirit of enterprise.
holidays.meaning: Vietnamese Entrepreneurs' Day honors those who dare to begin — from the market-stall trader to the tech founder. Entrepreneurs create not only wealth but jobs, confidence and the momentum of a country on the rise.

traditions.title: Business gatherings
traditions.text: On October 13, business associations — VCCI, chambers of commerce, young entrepreneur clubs — hold gatherings and CEO forums. It is the community's annual 'roll call' of health after each volatile year.

traditions.title: Startup forums
traditions.text: Around October 13 is startup-forum season: Techfest, Startup Day and founder-story talks draw young businesspeople. Entrepreneur Day has become the year's flagship moment for startup inspiration.

traditions.title: Company awards
traditions.text: The season brings respected prizes: the Thánh Gióng Cup for outstanding entrepreneurs, Sao Đỏ for community-minded firms, the VNR500 list of largest companies. The October 13 honors form the business world's annual 'gold board'.

traditions.title: Charitable work
traditions.text: Beyond awards, many corporations pick October 13 as a shared day of giving: scholarships, charity houses, healthcare sponsorships. 'Entrepreneurs do more than get rich' is the message repeated every year.

wishes: May Vietnamese entrepreneurs keep the startup fire — prosperous business ahead!
May Vietnam's business community stride firmly on the world stage!
Honoring the job-makers — may you trade well and keep a bright heart!
May Vietnamese startups fly high and Vietnamese brands resound far!
May those who dare to begin always be fairly rewarded!

gifts.title: Business books
gifts.text: Startup books and founder biographies — intellectual gifts for people in business.

gifts.title: Lucky plants
gifts.text: Money trees and 'fortune' plants — traditional gifts of luck.

gifts.title: Desk items
gifts.text: A signature pen, desk calendar or watch — formal gifts for entrepreneurs.

holidays.name: Vietnamese Communist Party Founding Day
holidays.tagline: The founding of the party that has led Vietnam's revolution.
holidays.meaning: The milestone that unified Vietnam's communist movement under a single leading party.

traditions.title: Anniversary ceremonies
traditions.text: Party committees from commune to central level hold solemn February 3 ceremonies: recalling the 1930 conference in Kowloon (Hong Kong) that merged the three communist organizations, reviewing nine-plus decades of history, and screening archival films.

traditions.title: New member induction
traditions.text: Founding Day is 'induction season': outstanding young people, soldiers and model workers are admitted as party members in solemn ceremonies — a moment each new member calls their 'second birthday'.

traditions.title: Volunteer campaigns
traditions.text: Local party cells run volunteer days around February 3: environmental clean-ups, tree planting, blood donation, visits to policy families. 'Every member a good deed' is the day's familiar slogan.

wishes: On the Party's founding day, may Vietnam stay united and prosperous.
Proud on February 3 — one nation, one spirit.
Wishing your party organization ever cleaner and stronger.
February 3 — remembering the oath beneath the flag, keeping the founding flame.
May the country keep rising on the path it chose, brilliant every spring.

gifts.title: Party history books
gifts.text: Documents and memoirs about the 1930 founding and the party congresses.

gifts.title: Flag pin
gifts.text: A national or party flag pin for a newly inducted member.

gifts.title: Heritage visit
gifts.text: A trip to sites tied to the founding conference or memorial houses of early leaders.

holidays.name: Điện Biên Phủ Victory Day
holidays.tagline: The victory that 'resounded across five continents and shook the earth'.
holidays.meaning: A symbol of the will to independence — the battle that brought a colonial power to the negotiating table.

traditions.title: Visiting A1 cemetery
traditions.text: The Điện Biên Phủ martyrs' cemetery on Hill D1 (Điện Biên Phủ city) welcomes veterans and descendants — busiest in the week of May 7. Wreaths and incense on the graves are the day's signature ritual.

traditions.title: Ceremonies in Điện Biên
traditions.text: The province holds annual commemorations; milestone years (60th, 65th, 70th) rise to state level — the 70th in 2024 featured parades and the largest exhibitions the Northwest has ever seen.

traditions.title: Archives and exhibitions
traditions.text: The Điện Biên Phủ Museum and libraries open archival displays: maps of De Castries' command bunker, soldiers' letters, photos of Corps 559 hauling artillery through the forest. On May 7 the documents 'come alive' for the public.

wishes: May 7 — proud of Điện Biên, proud of those who hauled cannons through jungle.
Honoring the heroic generation of Điện Biên Phủ — famed across five continents.
May the nation keep the peace its forebears bought with their lives.
56 days and nights for one mountain range — may the Điện Biên spirit live on.
Grateful for the past, worthy of the future — a meaningful May 7.

gifts.title: Books and films on the campaign
gifts.text: 'Điện Biên Phủ — a historic rendezvous' and material on General Võ Nguyên Giáp.

gifts.title: A trip to Điện Biên
gifts.text: Hill A1, De Castries' bunker, the war cemetery — an experience gift for the young.

gifts.title: Flowers for fallen soldiers
gifts.text: Lay flowers at a war memorial or martyrs' cemetery near you.

holidays.name: President Hồ Chí Minh's Birthday
holidays.tagline: The birthday of Uncle Hồ — beloved leader of the nation.
holidays.meaning: The day the nation turns its heart toward Kim Liên — honoring the man who went to find a road for his people.

traditions.title: Mausoleum visits
traditions.text: From early morning on May 19, thousands queue to enter the Mausoleum — every delegation in formal order, laying wreaths. His birthday is one of the Mausoleum's busiest days of the year, alongside September 2.

traditions.title: Pilgrimage to Kim Liên
traditions.text: Hoàng Trù–Kim Liên village (Nam Đàn, Nghệ An), where he was born, welcomes its biggest 'back to the roots' crowds on May 19: flowers at the thatched parental home, incense at the maternal home, ví-giặm folk singing all day.

traditions.title: Arts honoring him
traditions.text: Singing and storytelling contests about him bloom across schools and communes around May 19. Books, films and archives about his life are reintroduced to the young through the gentlest stories.

wishes: Honoring Uncle Hồ — the man who taught us to love our country with his whole life.
May 19 — may the spirit of 'nothing is more precious than independence and freedom' stay bright in every Vietnamese.
Live by his words: diligence, thrift, integrity, selflessness — a meaningful May 19.
Proud that our nation had Him — on his birthday, remember his teachings.
May every young Vietnamese carry some of Uncle Hồ's will to rise.

gifts.title: A mausoleum visit
gifts.text: Take family or students to Ba Đình to visit the mausoleum and the Presidential Palace grounds.

gifts.title: Books about him
gifts.text: Prison Diary, his poetry, biographies — meaningful gifts for the young.

gifts.title: Tickets to commemorative shows
gifts.text: Art programs and poetry nights for May 19 at the Hanoi Opera House and in the provinces.

holidays.name: August Revolution Day
holidays.tagline: The day Hanoi seized power, opening the era of independence.
holidays.meaning: History's handover moment — from more than eighty years of colonization to national independence.

traditions.title: Ceremonies at the Opera House
traditions.text: The Hanoi Opera House — where the August 19, 1945 rally gathered hundreds of thousands to hear the call to the General Uprising — hosts the official ceremony each year. The square in front, now called August Revolution Square, is the day's 'red address'.

traditions.title: Parades and flags
traditions.text: The capital's streets fly red flags all week; youth delegations march with the banner 'Nothing is more precious than independence and freedom' through the walking streets. Provinces tie the day to their own revolutionary tradition dates.

traditions.title: Traditional activities
traditions.text: Organizations and schools hold 'August stories' sessions: the columns advancing on Hanoi, the bronze bugle of the uprising, village elders leading communes to take power. August 19 is also the tradition day of the People's Police.

wishes: Proud of August! May the nation forever keep the flag of independence raised then.
August 19 — remembering the day Hanoi rose; wishing the land everlasting peace.
The August Revolution teaches: when a nation rises, nothing can stop it — a meaningful anniversary.
May today's youth be worthy of those who won back the country in 1945.
Another August 19 — respectfully offering gratitude to those who went before.

gifts.title: Books on the August Revolution
gifts.text: Material on the General Uprising, Tân Trào and the historic days of late August 1945.

gifts.title: Opera House visit
gifts.text: A trip to August Revolution Square — the site of the August 19 rally.

gifts.title: Hanoi 1945 photo sets
gifts.text: Black-and-white archival photos of the day Hanoi seized power — a gift for history lovers.

holidays.name: Hanoi Liberation Day
holidays.tagline: The day the red flag with gold star flew again over Hanoi's citadel.
holidays.meaning: The day Hanoi returned to the nation's hands — closing one page of history to open a new one for the capital and the country.

traditions.title: Ceremonies in Hanoi
traditions.text: The city-level ceremony is held at the National Convention Center or the Opera House; the 70th anniversary in 2024 was the capital's biggest event with parades, exhibitions and the concert 'Hanoi — faith and hope'.

traditions.title: Streets ablaze with flags
traditions.text: The Old Quarter floods with flags around October 10 — flags over ancient tiled roofs, along Hàng Đào–Hàng Ngang where the liberation columns entered in 1954. Tourism bodies run 'in the footsteps of the takeover' tours for visitors.

traditions.title: 'Hanoi remembers' exhibitions
traditions.text: The Hanoi Museum and book-street exhibitions show 'the takeover days': bicycles carrying soldiers, shops reopening on the first morning, family letters bearing the news. The 'stories of those who stayed' are always the most-read section.

wishes: October 10 — may Hanoi forever be the nation's proud heart.
Remembering the day flags covered every street — wishing the capital more flowers, the country more peace.
Hanoi Liberation Day — gratitude to the soldiers who took over the city that year.
May thousand-year Hanoi keep its elegance and serenity.
Proud to be a child of the capital — a meaningful October 10.

gifts.title: Books and old maps of Hanoi
gifts.text: Material on the takeover, 1954 maps of Hanoi, archival photos of the five gates.

gifts.title: Visit the Flag Tower
gifts.text: The Kỳ đài inside the Thăng Long Imperial Citadel — where the flag rose on October 10.

gifts.title: October 10 art programs
gifts.text: Tickets to concerts, plays and film screenings marking Liberation Day.

holidays.name: Vietnam Book and Reading Culture Day
holidays.tagline: A day honoring books and the reading habit of the Vietnamese.
holidays.meaning: A reminder that reading is the most durable way to grow knowledge — and a push toward a true 'reading culture' for the whole society.

traditions.title: Shared reading hour
traditions.text: Every April 21 a nationwide 'shared reading hour' takes place — schools, offices and libraries pause for 15–30 minutes to read together. The campaign spreads from provinces down to schools and reading communities.

traditions.title: Book fairs & festivals
traditions.text: Book week around April 21 blooms with fairs: HCMC's Book Street, Hanoi's 19/12 Book Street, children's book festivals — deep discounts, author meet-ups, 'books that changed the world' displays. Many provinces hold their first-ever fairs on this date.

traditions.title: Donating books
traditions.text: Charities and schools run 'book-donation weeks': collecting used books for the highlands, building classroom shelves, funding commune libraries. April 21 is also when families pick 'a reading tradition' for their children.

traditions.title: Launches & author talks
traditions.text: Publishers time new titles for Reading Day — author-reader meetups in bookstores and livestreams. The April 21 'meet the author' sessions draw young readers queuing for signatures.

wishes: April 21 — may a good book always wait on your nightstand.
Every turned page opens a new horizon — may you never run out of horizons.
Wishing your family a Book Day full of rustling pages.
A reader lives a thousand lives — wishing you a thousand interesting ones.
May your children grow up beside the family's warm bookshelf.

gifts.title: A well-matched book
gifts.text: Giving a book is giving a world — pick the topic they care about most.

gifts.title: A nice bookmark or reading lamp
gifts.text: A small but genuinely useful gift for late-night readers.

gifts.title: Book voucher / ebook subscription
gifts.text: Let them choose — the safest gift for a picky bookworm.

holidays.name: Vietnam Sports Day
holidays.tagline: A day honoring the nation's spirit of physical training.
holidays.meaning: Inscribing Uncle Hồ's words 'healthy to work' — every healthy citizen is a share of the nation's strength.

traditions.title: Olympic Run
traditions.text: The Olympic Run for Public Health — a 30-plus-year tradition — is held on the Sunday nearest March 27 at hundreds of simultaneous starting points nationwide. From pupils to grandparents, everyone runs 'for health' — the day's finest picture.

traditions.title: Morning exercise
traditions.text: Sports Day recalls Hồ Chí Minh's 'morning exercise' appeal — parks on the morning of March 27 are livelier than usual with qigong classes, folk dance and free public yoga.

traditions.title: Grassroots tournaments
traditions.text: The Phù Đổng Children's Games, commune fun-runs and inter-office badminton — the 'whole people train following his example' movement peaks in March. Sports Day opens the amateur season for the year.

traditions.title: Honoring achievements
traditions.text: The sector uses the date to honor medalists of SEA Games, ASIAD and the Olympics. March 27 was chosen because on March 27, 1946 Hồ Chí Minh signed the decree founding Vietnamese sport.

wishes: March 27 — stay fit like an athlete, play hard, live fully.
Wishing your family a joyful workout each morning and a healthy body each year.
To Vietnamese sports — may our flag-wearing athletes keep soaring on world stages.
Healthy to work, to love, to live — wishing you an energetic Sports Day.
May your team win this weekend — and win against tomorrow's morning laziness too.

gifts.title: Running shoes / workout gear
gifts.text: A gift that nudges someone to start moving.

gifts.title: Sports tickets
gifts.text: A football match, badminton meet or martial-arts event — watching feeds the sporting spirit.

gifts.title: Home training gear
gifts.text: Pull-up bar, dumbbells, yoga mat — practical for anyone too busy for the gym.

holidays.name: Vietnam Law Day
holidays.tagline: A day honoring the law and bringing it to every citizen.
holidays.meaning: A reminder of modern society's most basic principle: the state governs by law — and no one stands above it.

traditions.title: Legal outreach
traditions.text: On November 9, 'law day' outreach is the core activity: lawyer teams hand out leaflets on new laws, legal banners go up everywhere, and training classes on the Land Law and Marriage Law open in every commune.

traditions.title: Free legal aid
traditions.text: Free legal-aid booths appear at pagodas, communal halls and admin centers: volunteer lawyers answer questions on land, labor and divorce — the issues people ask most. It is the day's most practical activity.

traditions.title: Law quizzes in schools
traditions.text: Schools run 'learn the law' contests with everyday scenarios: riding without a helmet, labor contracts, social media conduct — students learn law through games instead of lectures.

traditions.title: Honoring legal workers
traditions.text: The justice sector holds tradition meetings honoring drafters, judges, lawyers and legal officers — and recalls November 9, 1946, when the first National Assembly passed Vietnam's first constitution.

wishes: November 9 — may you live truly free within clearly drawn bounds.
Know the law to protect yourself; respect the law to protect each other — have a meaningful Law Day.
To lawmakers — may you always hold the scales of justice steady.
The law is the shield of the weak — may it always be raised in time.
Wishing your family a peaceful day — the kind only a law-abiding society can have.

gifts.title: A popular-law book
gifts.text: 'Law for non-lawyers' titles — a surprisingly practical gift.

gifts.title: A legal consultation
gifts.text: A session with a lawyer for someone tangled in paperwork, contracts or land matters.

gifts.title: National Assembly heritage visit
gifts.text: Stop by the National Assembly Museum — where the first constitution was passed.

holidays.name: Vietnam Trade Day
holidays.tagline: A day honoring commerce and Vietnamese goods reaching the world.
holidays.meaning: Honoring everyone in commerce — from the market vendor to the exporting enterprise — the trade that carried Vietnamese goods and the words 'Viet Nam' onto the world map.

traditions.title: Trade fairs
traditions.text: Around July 13 and through the summer comes fair season: Vietnam Expo, VietFood and provincial fairs — booths of genuine 'Vietnamese goods' displaying export products and each locality's OCOP specialties. It is the 'festival' of the nation's trade front.

traditions.title: Honoring businesses
traditions.text: Trade Day honors export achievers: 'trusted exporter' awards and top FDI exporters — where October 13 honors the entrepreneur as a person, this day honors the trading organization.

traditions.title: Trade seminars
traditions.text: The Ministry of Industry and Trade and export associations hold seminars around the date: EU–US–Japan market trends, tapping EVFTA, cross-border e-commerce — the hottest questions of Vietnamese exports.

traditions.title: Vietnamese-goods week
traditions.text: 'Vietnamese Goods Week' and the 'Vietnamese people prioritize Vietnamese goods' campaign run for the occasion: supermarkets discount domestic products and regional specialty fairs bring 'Made in Vietnam' to Vietnamese shoppers first.

wishes: July 13 — may traders meet fortune: easy buying, brisk selling, wealth flowing.
May Vietnamese trade keep reaching further — goods to every continent.
Wishing your business full order books, steady payments and trusted partners.
Prosperity in trade, prosperity in wealth — a smooth year of commerce to you.
From the village market stall to the export container — may every Vietnamese 'seller' stand firm.

gifts.title: Quality Vietnamese goods
gifts.text: Pick a 'made in Vietnam' gift over imports — support trade with your own wallet.

gifts.title: Specialty coffee & tea
gifts.text: Two world-famous Vietnamese exports — gifts for partners at home and abroad.

gifts.title: A fair visit
gifts.text: Take family to a trade fair — see with your own eyes how far Vietnamese goods have traveled.

holidays.name: Ho Chi Minh Communist Youth Union Day
holidays.tagline: The founding anniversary of Vietnam's largest youth organization.
holidays.meaning: A day reminding young people of a ninety-year tradition of stepping forward — from Ly Tu Trong to the volunteer brigades, to today's green summer campaigns and startups.

traditions.title: New member ceremonies
traditions.text: Founding Day is the 'finest day' for Union inductions: ninth-graders stand before the Union flag and recite the pledge — a first 'growing-up' moment many remember all their lives.

traditions.title: Youth Month
traditions.text: Since 2004, March has been 'Youth Month': volunteer building, blood donation, tree planting, beach clean-ups — the nation's young people take the field in the same blue shirts. March 26 crowns that month of activity.

traditions.title: Tradition gatherings
traditions.text: Solemn ceremonies retell Union history from March 26, 1931 in Vinh, remembering Lý Tự Trọng — the first member to die, at just 17 — and reuniting generations of Union members.

traditions.title: Volunteer building
traditions.text: Union-built 'youth roads', rural bridges and cultural houses are the tradition's signature output: from the legendary Hồ Chí Minh road to today's 'Union to the countryside' village lanes.

wishes: March 26 — may your youth always have a front line of your own to step up to.
Wishing every union member keeps the fire of zeal — in lecture halls, labs, or remote villages.
Youth doesn't wait — may your founding day be busy and memorable.
May Vietnamese youth keep writing the 'xung kich' tradition in creativity and volunteering.
To members old and new: thank you for the green summers and volunteer trips — March 26 is yours.

gifts.title: Union badge & member card
gifts.text: A small but meaningful keepsake for someone newly inducted.

gifts.title: Volunteer t-shirt
gifts.text: The green 'Mua he xanh' or red spring-volunteer shirt — the uniform of 'xung kich' youth.

gifts.title: Books on young heroes
gifts.text: Stories of Ly Tu Trong and Vo Thi Sau — reminding youth that 17–20 is old enough to matter.

holidays.name: Vietnam Poetry Day
holidays.tagline: The first full-moon night reserved for Vietnamese poetry.
holidays.meaning: Honoring poetry — the art form longest bound to Vietnamese culture: from lullaby folk verse and Tang-regulated poems to The Tale of Kieu and modern free verse.

traditions.title: Van Mieu poetry night
traditions.text: The Poetry Night at Văn Miếu – Quốc Tử Giám unfolds on the first-full-moon evening by the Well of Literature beneath the Khuê Văn pavilion: great poets, children and folk singers read by candlelight and moonlight — the nation's grandest night of verse.

traditions.title: Reading together
traditions.text: Poetry cafés, verse clubs and schools hold their own 'poetry hour': each person brings a beloved poem to read aloud. For one night, Vietnamese verse becomes a true community activity.

traditions.title: Annual theme
traditions.text: Each year the Vietnam Writers' Association sets a theme for Poetry Day — 'Poetry and homeland', 'Poetry of spring' — and the week's contests and exhibitions revolve around it.

traditions.title: Honoring poets
traditions.text: The day also celebrates beloved poets and awards the year's verse prizes — Nguyễn Du, Xuân Quỳnh and the 'humanist' generation are recalled; many children hear their own voices recite before a crowd for the first time.

wishes: First full moon — may your year slow down just enough to hear the meter of your own life.
May your blank page stay open and full — like tonight's moon.
On Poetry Day — may those who write keep writing, and those who love poetry keep loving it.
May you find a line this year that only you fully understand.
To the poets: thank you for making the Vietnamese language more beautiful, word by word — this full moon is yours.

gifts.title: A poetry collection
gifts.text: A fine edition of The Tale of Kieu, or a book by a poet you love — the most on-theme gift possible.

gifts.title: Notebook & fountain pen
gifts.text: To begin the first verse — a gift for someone who wants to write.

gifts.title: Poetry night tickets
gifts.text: The experience of verse under the full moon — a gift that needs no wrapping.

holidays.name: International Men's Day
holidays.tagline: A day to thank the men in our lives.
holidays.meaning: A thank-you to men who rarely hear it — a day to pay attention to men's health, emotions and roles in society.

traditions.title: Wishes for men
traditions.text: Children, wives and partners send November 19 wishes to fathers, husbands and brothers — the day is not yet as big as March 8 but grows more familiar each year: 'stay healthy, Dad' is the classic message.

traditions.title: Health themes
traditions.text: Each International Men's Day carries a men's-health theme: prostate cancer, male mental health — tied to the global Movember movement growing mustaches through November for men's-health causes.

traditions.title: Honoring role models
traditions.text: The day honors positive male role models: single fathers raising children, devoted male nurses, men who have donated blood a hundred times — 'good men worth knowing' are sought out and their stories retold.

traditions.title: Paired with March 8
traditions.text: In Vietnam, November 19 is often treated as the day men 'receive back' what March 8 gives women — a dinner cooked by the man himself, a gift for Dad. Though unofficial, it is slowly becoming a new cultural habit.

wishes: November 19 — wishing the men in your life good health, and the courage to say when they're tired.
To the quiet fathers: thank you for a lifetime of silent shoulders.
To brothers, uncles and friends — may you be loved as clearly as the women in your family are.
May every man find a full night's sleep — and someone to talk to when it matters.
On Men's Day — may you live up to the example the kids around you would want to follow.

gifts.title: A health checkup
gifts.text: A screening appointment or checkup package — the most practical gift for someone who skips the doctor.

gifts.title: Sports gear
gifts.text: Running shoes, gym gloves, a jump rope — encouragement for an active habit.

gifts.title: Quality personal items
gifts.text: A watch, leather wallet, grooming set — things men often skimp on for themselves.
